UN R999 (version 2.1.0)

Consolidated text of this version, rendered by Certivity for the hackathon.

Role in the hackathon: base version.

Introduction

This made-up Regulation exists to test how regulation PDFs are split into paragraphs.

1. Scope

1.1. This Regulation applies to test lamps of category T.1

1 As defined in the Consolidated Resolution on test lamps.

1.2. This Regulation does not apply to:

1.2.1. Lamps that are not tested;

1.2.3. Lamps that are tested twice.

2. Definitions

For the purposes of this Regulation:

2.1. "Test lamp" means a lamp that is tested.

2.2. "Category T" means the category of test lamps.

5. Specifications

5.1. Photometric requirements

5.1.1. The luminous intensity shall not exceed 30 cd above the horizontal plane described in paragraph
5.3. of this Regulation, measured as in UN Regulation No.
149. Lamps of category T are measured once.

5.1.2. The intensity distribution shall be measured at the following points:
Point 01 at 0 degrees
Point 02 at 1 degree
Point 03 at 2 degrees
Point 04 at 3 degrees
Point 05 at 4 degrees
Point 06 at 5 degrees
Point 07 at 6 degrees
Point 08 at 7 degrees
Point 09 at 8 degrees

Point 29 at 28 degrees
Point 30 at 29 degrees

1Minimum intensity0.3 cd
2Maximum intensity30 cd

5.2. The colour of the light shall be red.

6. Transitional provisions

6.1. No Contracting Party shall refuse approvals under this version.

Annex 1 Communication

(Maximum format: A4 (210 x 297 mm))

1. Name of the manufacturer: ........

2. Type of lamp: ........

Annex 2 Test procedures

Part 1 - Resistance to heat

1. Test procedure

1.1. The lamp shall be kept for 48 hours at 65 °C.

2. After this test, no cracking shall be visible.

Part 2 - Resistance to water

1. The lamp shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water.

Annex 2 - Appendix 1 Test report

1. Report number: ........

Annex 9 K Fire resistance

1. The lamp shall not burn.
